title: The Whole System on One Page
lede: Six steps, one list, one message on every channel. I want you to see the whole thing before you build any one piece of it.
deliverable: The whole outreach system in your head.
body:
Once, at the start of the module. Every Jarvis step in this module needs them.

Give Jarvis this module’s skills

Download jarvis-skills-module-4-outreach.zip from this lesson, attach it in your Jarvis chat and send the message below. Jarvis installs every skill in the file and tells you the first step. If Jarvis says an earlier step comes first, do that step. It’ll tell you when to come back.

Install Module 4, Outreach, from the attached file. Add every skill inside, replace any older versions, and don't run anything yet. When you're done, show me what you installed and where we start.

Before continuing: Jarvis lists all 6 skills with a version next to each.

In this module, you’ll use Jarvis to find businesses that fit your offer, identify the right person and prepare your outreach. You’ll learn how to use calls, email, LinkedIn and messages together.

You’re turning your offer into real conversations with business owners. Each message and follow-up should build on the last, with everything tracked in your CRM.

By the end, you’ll have a researched prospect list, relevant outreach, call scripts and a follow-up plan ready to run. Outreach and paid ads are two acquisition routes; you can start with either.

Ads are how I have always got clients. Outreach is the system we run on our own offer, written down step by step so you can run it on yours. You can start with manual outreach before adding paid tools.

Why speak with owners

Speaking with owners helps you hear how they describe the problem, what they have tried and whether your offer lands. Outreach lets you start those conversations directly. You can also start with paid ads; either way, track the conversations and use what you learn to improve the offer.

The six steps

  1. Tell Jarvis the account. Not "plumbers". Plumbing businesses in Brisbane with three or more vans, who miss calls because everyone is on the tools. Industry, place, size, pain.
  2. Jarvis builds the list from Google Maps. Name, phone, address, website, hours, rating, reviews. Three hundred businesses in an afternoon, on Google's free allowance, in any country.
  3. Jarvis reads every website. Owner's name, email, how they take bookings, rough staff count, and the signs of your pain: no online booking, no after hours answer, a job ad for an admin.
  4. Jarvis finds the owner. Every country has a free business registry: ABN Lookup, Companies House, your state's business search. You call a name, not a switchboard. Top accounts with nothing in the registry, you look up on LinkedIn by hand.
  5. Jarvis ranks them and writes the message. Pain signs, size, reachability. You read the top thirty yourself. Then one message, one angle, adapted to each channel: call script, email, LinkedIn note, DM.
  6. You run it. Dial the listed number. Email from your own business mailbox through your CRM. LinkedIn and DMs by hand. Three touches a week for three weeks, every touch logged. A reply, a booking or a "stop" ends the sequence on every channel.

The numbers

Two five figure deals a month needs about seven first calls. If a good list books one call in twenty, that is around 140 accounts a month, so Jarvis ranks 400 to 600 raw accounts. Track accounts, conversations, first calls booked, attended, second calls, deals won, cash in. Your CRM shows it on one card.

Paid data tools

They find more emails and they are faster past a few hundred accounts a month. Nobody gives you reliable mobiles, so you dial the listed number either way. Past a few hundred accounts a month, upgrade to a paid data tool. Until then, do not spend a dollar on data.

The rules

  • A scraped mobile number is not permission to text it. SMS only where your country's rules allow it and the person has a reason to hear from you.
  • Every email has your real name, your business and a way to opt out.
  • A reply, a booking or a "stop" ends the sequence everywhere, the same day.
  • Cold email from one business inbox is fine at this volume. Never buy a list and blast it. That burns a domain you need for the next five years.
